sources.notes: Two 10 km items supply the 1 m EPSG:3006/RH 2000 DTM because the course straddles E 680000: 662_67 (checksum above, captured 2021-04-17) and 662_68 (09e2d304f7d8778c9c1e1a099d4ab0733860a218ebaccfded2e167a6675a2632, captured 2023-05-16 within a 2021-04-17..2025-06-13 range). The acquired window is the 2049 by 2049 sample lattice at E678403.5/N6626324.5, Float32 sha256 e51bcc0a915c12164c8f94d9bfc30eebd1af709db94f8fb6e307d53e2f2c423c. The two vintages leave NO measurable step at their boundary: the across-seam first difference is mean 0.075 m against 0.082 and 0.085 m for control columns either side. Advertised uncertainty is not an independent course residual, so canonical-origin approval remains pending.

sources.notes: 74 authenticated RGBI review windows cover both courses and estate facilities. Native source pixels are 0.16 m; whole-hole context is 0.32 m and the estate overview is 0.8 m. Published mosaic seam metadata dates all acquired pixels to 2025-06-14. Reviewed vector corrections are applied before both compatibility models are written. Raw imagery remains in the ignored local cache. Ground sample distance is not absolute positional accuracy; no independent horizontal controls or daily tee-colour survey are claimed.

One campaign, 21C039, ALS80-HP, flown 2021-04-17 LEAF-OFF at 1.2 pulses/m2 declared (2.5-2.6 all returns/m2 measured). The checksum identifies item 21c039-662_67, whose COPC is read by bounded octree range request and never downloaded whole. Items 21c039-662_67 and 21c039-662_68 meet at E 680000 inside the course, but both belong to the same campaign so there is no vintage seam to reconcile. Leaf-off under-detects deciduous crowns; see the canopy-source audit for how much.

Checksummed official STAC selection for both courses on this ground: DTM, Laserdata Skog and orto-o2-2025 each cover the AOI completely. The AOI bbox was projected with the repository Kruger series rather than PROJ (no toolchain on the acquiring machine); the file records that, and no published coordinate derives from it.

The authenticated 1 m window read for the published graph: items, ETags, byte counts, the exact sample lattice and pixel-edge window, and the finite/plausibility statistics. Read at overview factor 1, so every published sample is a source pixel copied exactly.

The MEASURED legacy-to-RH-2000 step used by the runtime bridge: median 5.6676 m over 38,543 mown-ground samples, MAD 1.7211 m. The spread is a coarse global model disagreeing with a laser DTM about terrain shape, not misregistration -- a +/-40 m registration sweep over four bridge variants moves it by under 0.25 m. It is a datum step, not a claim that the two surfaces agree.
Pinned Laserdata Skog inventory: one active campaign 21C039 over both items, capture dates, densities, the E 680000 item seam and licence terms.

COPC headers and hierarchy pages only, no point bytes. Combined AOI density 1.59-4.21 all returns/m2 with no empty window. Item 662_67 is a 5 km HALF-tile whose COPC cube does not span its header extent, which is why node selection follows the extent rule and not the cube.

Per-tile canopy rasters derived from class 2/9 ground and height above ground. The cloud ground minus the published DTM has a median of 0.00 m on every one of the 64 tiles, which is an independent confirmation of the published terrain.
Meta/WRI CHMv2 tile 1200312031 sampled onto the campaign rasters own 1 m lattice. Independent optical sensor, used as calibration.

Laser 17.6% canopy, CHMv2 27.9%, legacy Esri raster 43.9%. Where the Esri raster claims canopy and the laser does not (106,626 cells) the laser height is median 0.00 m and p90 0.36 m, i.e. open ground the satellite over-detected rather than crowns the leaf-off scan lost.
